notable_absence.finding: This page's AsciiDoc `{sgw}` attribute reference was never resolved before publication - it appears literally as the four characters `{sgw}` at least eight times in running prose ('{sgw} uses a reserved system collection...', 'From {sgw} 4.1, you can opt in...', '{sgw} triggers this function...', '{sgw} creates no replicas of indexes...'). Every other page in this batch spells out 'Sync Gateway' in full; this is the only page in the batch with the raw, unrendered attribute leaking through, a genuine publishing defect worth a docs-issue at reconciliation time.

cross_component_finding: This page's stated limit - 'You can define 1 custom scope per database with up to 1000 custom collections' (repeated verbatim twice on this page) - phrases the collection cap as PER DATABASE, while configuration-schema-database.json's Table/limits section states '1000 custom collections across the cluster' - a CLUSTER-wide cap. These are materially different constraints (a cluster with many databases could exhaust a cluster-wide 1000 far sooner than a per-database 1000 would suggest) and no page reconciles the discrepancy; both quotes are recorded faithfully on their respective records rather than silently normalized to one reading.
cross_product_finding: None beyond what is already established (sgw:custom-scope, sgw:custom-collection, sgw:system-metadata-collection) elsewhere in this batch - this page is entirely about Sync Gateway's own database-configuration surface, with worked JavaScript examples reusing access-control primitives (access(), channel(), requireRole()) already modeled from round 3.
